title: indian shares likely open higher ahead rbi rate decision 2026 08 05
text:
Aug 5 (Reuters) - Indian benchmarks ended in the green on Wednesday, after the central bank held rates as expected, while a rise in crude oil prices on ​lingering Mideast uncertainty kept a lid on gains.
The benchmark Nifty 50 (.NSEI)
, opens new tab
 rose ‌0.04% to 26,624.65 and the Sensex (.BSESN)
, opens new tab
 added 0.19% to 78,581 points.
The indexes have been showing some divergence this week since the launch of a new closing auction for pricing indexes. Before close at 3:15 p.m. IST, ​the Nifty was down 0.18% and the Sensex was up 0.09%.
India's markets regulator ​sees no structural or design flaws in the new auction system and ⁠has set no timeline for a review, Reuters reported, citing a source.
Brent rose to $80.7 per ​barrel after Houthi attacks on a Saudi tanker clouded prospects for de-escalation in the five-month-long Iran ​war.
Reserve Bank of India Governor Sanjay Malhotra said that inflation has moved above target mainly because of higher fuel prices, while broader price pressures remained in check.
Signalling no rush to act until there is ​greater clarity on inflation, Malhotra reaffirmed the RBI's "resolute" commitment to the inflation target.
"We read the ​policy as dovish, and any decision to hike rates will be significantly influenced by external circumstances, in ‌our ⁠view," said analysts led by Suresh Ganapathy of Macquarie.
"We do not envisage a rate hike in 2026, which is negative for banks' margin outlook and positive for non-bank lenders."
India's largest private lenders, HDFC Bank (HDBK.NS)
, opens new tab
 and ICICI Bank (ICBK.NS)
, opens new tab
, fell 0.9% and 0.3%, dragging banks (.NSEBANK)
, opens new tab
 0.3% lower.
Nine of ​the 16 major ​sectors declined.
Small-caps (.NIFSMCP100)
, opens new tab
 ⁠rose 0.8% to a record high, while mid-caps (.NIFMDCP100)
, opens new tab
 came off all-time highs to close 0.2% higher.
"Investors are seeing opportunity in broader mid- ​and small-caps where momentum, strong earnings outlook and concentration of domestic mutual-fund ​flows are ⁠aiding an uptick," said Todd McClone, portfolio manager at William Blair Investment Management.
"If foreign money starts coming in on top of that, those areas could see a meaningful boost going forward," ⁠McClone said.
Among ​stocks, PNB Housing (PNBH.NS)
, opens new tab
 rose 3.9% to a 23-month high ​after reporting higher quarterly profit.
Bharti Hexacom (BHAX.NS)
, opens new tab
 fell 4% as analysts flagged weaker-than-expected subscriber additions in the June quarter.
